svg.title: 2 ∑︁ z |P(z) − Q(z)|. One validation observation is a complete B-copy experiment; source-copy cost is B times the number of such observations. The proof filtration contains completed experiment records and their mathematically defined scoring truths. During trusted validation the evaluator can use the known preparation label; the reader remains adapted only to its permitted record subfiltration. Conditional source, response and tube promises are imposed on this augmented past, including admitted timing metadata. They do not follow merely by enlarging a smaller observed-history filtration. In the structured four-state comparisons, each new experiment draws an independent uniform root seed conditional on the completed past and its chosen label. The unrestricted-record and general trusted-seed models state their own ancillary-law promises instead. Structured block drift averages over its fresh seed; local likelihood validity is pointwise once the seed and command are known. No future validation-success event is conditioned on as initial information.
